diagram_math_checks.details: For fixed N,n,a and supplied inverse, f_a and f_ainverse are total functions {0,1}^{n+1} -> {0,1}^n, including invalid data encodings. Each compiled oracle preserves its (c,current data) input, XORs an n-bit value into t, and returns its work to zero. The displayed basis states have register lengths 1,n,n,w. This follows from Definition input/function clauses, final compilation paragraph, def-qc-coherent-function-oracle, and alg-qc-reversible-embedding steps 1-4.
With t=0^n, O_fa sends (c,z,0^n,0^w) to (c,z,z′,0^w), z′=f_a(c,z), by the clean-target XOR convention. The work is zero at both block boundaries, not asserted to stay zero inside the block.

The second arrow swaps only the n-bit data and target registers, yielding (c,z′,z,0^w). Per corresponding bit pair, target XOR data, data XOR target, target XOR data yields (u,v)->(u,u XOR v)->(v,u XOR v)->(v,u). Corresponding pairs preserve each register’s most-significant-first port order; time is explicitly downward. This is the algorithm’s final compilation paragraph and correctness proof step 4.1.

For c=1,z<N, z′=az mod N lies below N and f_ainverse(c,z′)=a^{-1}az mod N=z. For c=0 or z>=N, both total functions return z, so again f_ainverse(c,z′)=z. Thus the final oracle XORs z into the target holding old z and produces 0^n, preserving c,z′ and restoring work. These are the precise piecewise definition and correctness proof steps 3.1 and 5.1; O_fainverse is labeled as the oracle of the inverse function, not as the inverse of O_fa.

The existing algorithm and separate correctness proof were preserved in full and do not use the new figure. Supplemental finite state check passed 137572 basis inputs: all N=2..64, all units a, both controls, all n-bit encodings; checked range, inverse-function cleanup, identity branches and the three-CNOT swap. This finite check supplements the algebraic explanation and is not a full circuit-DAG audit.
